blocks.cap: 3:11am, a text that doesn't sound like anyone trying to sound like anything

blocks.p: At 3:11 the phone lit the ceiling white, and the buzz against the pillow went through his skull like a dentist's drill.
It was the dead hour, when even Tokyo has the decency to dim. Rei had fallen asleep in his clothes. He came up out of a dream about water and had the phone in his hand before he knew he was awake.
There was no greeting and no small name and no warmth aimed anywhere.
dont come to kita dont come here its not him answering rei i can feel it making the wall thin go to itsuki burn the

It stopped there. No punctuation. The sentence was cut off the way the journal's fourteenth-of-August entry was cut off, mid-act, a hand pulled off a page. The typos were wrong in the right way. They were Gin's typos, the leftward stumble of a man who had never learned to thumb-type cleanly. Autocorrect refused. Panic in the missing capitals.
Rei had spent the whole night learning that the smooth voice was the enemy. And here was the broken one, and his heart went through the floor toward it like a stone down a well.
He sat up in the dark with the phone too bright in his hand and read it nine times.

Everything in him that was a brother wanted to be on the first train to Kita-ku. That contradicted the very text that begged him not to come. And if the thing wearing Gin wanted him away from Kita, then the broken voice telling him to stay away might be the thing too. Except that the broken voice had named the thinning of the wall. It had confessed the plan. It had pointed him at Itsuki and at burning something. A gatekeeper does not hand over the location of its own gate.

Unless. Unless the most patient version of the trap was one that let the trapped man surface for exactly one message. A brother who has been forbidden will run toward the forbidden place faster than any brother merely invited.
He could feel the precise shape of the hope and the precise shape of the hook sitting on the same coordinates. He could not pull them apart by wanting to.

He reached for the Archive on the floor beside the mattress, where he had left it at dawn. He did not need to search. He knew the page now. It was in the chapter on demons, at the end of the list of tells, in a box Gin had marked urgent.

doc.title: Gin's book. Chapter Nine. Urgent comment.
lines: The secondary signal in partial possession. I want to state this as clearly as the documentation allows. The host is still there.

The four seconds where the host surfaces are the most important four seconds of the encounter. They confirm the host is present. They may carry information. They are almost certainly the only communication the host can manage.
Do not miss them by only reading the dominant signal. Look for the secondary.

blocks.p: A few seconds of thumbs. That was what a man could manage, from inside, when the thing driving him looked away. Gin had used his few seconds to type a warning, a place, a friend's name and half of an instruction.
Rei turned back a few pages to the part he had skimmed the first time, because he had not wanted it to be about anyone he knew.

doc.title: Gin's book. Chapter Six. Possession. The Two States.
lines: Partial possession. The demon occupies and drives the host body while the host soul remains inside. The host is conscious, aware, experiencing everything done through their body, but cannot surface except under specific conditions and cannot control their own actions. The demon uses the host's memories and relationships as cover. The host is trapped, not gone.
This state is unstable. It progresses over time toward full possession as the demon's hold deepens and the host's resistance wears down.

Full possession, or soul ejection. The demon completes the fusion and forces the host soul out entirely, into the Threshold. The soul has witnessed the whole of the partial possession, and in that state it turns heavily toward the Demon or Suffering Being paths. The body goes on under complete demon control. The host is gone.
After ejection the demon can still be removed from the body, but the host must then be found and guided in the Threshold before their path sets. That is a different and much harder operation.
Exorcism during partial possession is the recovery with the best outcome. The host returns changed. They carry the memory of the whole duration. They do not return undamaged. They return.

blocks.p: They return. Rei read the two words until they stopped being words. Gin was in the first state. He had to be. Someone who had been forced out could not have reached for a phone. But Gin's own page said the first state did not stay the first state. It deepened. Every message the smooth voice sent was a little more of the hold settling, and every moment Gin managed to surface cost him something he might not get back.

The seasickness was back, his own floor tilting. For once he was grateful for it, because it meant he was still reading and not yet decided. He checked himself the way the Running Low page said to. Did he feel reachable, as if a door were open somewhere? No. Only tired, and frightened, and hungry. He made himself get up, eat a cold rice ball from the fridge standing at the counter, and drink a glass of water. Gin would have said that before anything else. Eat. Sleep. He could not sleep. He could eat.

Out the window the last Obon lanterns had guttered along the canal. The dead were presumably guided home. The living were left holding their phones. He did not text back yet. He made himself be a person who waited sixty seconds. He watched the screen for the smooth voice to come and clean up after the broken one.

blocks.cap: What the smooth voice does next, and the tell in how fast it comes

blocks.p: At 3:16 the smooth voice arrived. The speed of it told him more than any sentence could.
I'm sorry... I don't even know what I wrote, I think I fell asleep texting, I've been so tired. Ignore that, please. I'm fine. Don't go anywhere on account of a half-asleep message.

It was reasonable. In its way it was even true. Fatigue, confusion, a man not himself. And it was fast. It was fast in the way the earlier replies had never been fast, fast like something that had been caught and was now working. The warmth in it was pointed harder than usual. There was more please in it, more aim.

The broken text had said burn and Itsuki and the wall. The smooth text would like him to file all three under sleeplessness and go back to bed. He had learned tonight whose interest each of those served.

Holding the two messages five minutes apart, he understood that he had just watched the seam happen live. It was not in a journal recovered after the fact. It was not in handwriting studied cold. It was happening in real time. The older voice had surfaced for a few broken seconds, and the newer one had rushed in to plaster over the gap.

The thing had not denied the plan. It could not deny it fast enough, because the leftward voice had already said the plan out loud. So it did the next thing, the thing it was best at. It reframed the confession as a symptom, and offered him the comfort of disbelieving his own brother. That was the whole technique, he saw now. It did not fight his love for Gin. It enlisted it. It asked his love to please be reasonable, and to please not make a tired man feel watched.
He put the phone face-down on the floor where he could not see the next message arrive. He breathed. He let the certainty assemble itself slowly, so that it would be certainty and not just wanting.

Gin was in there. He had surfaced. It had cost him something to surface, and it had cost the thing something to bury him. The burying had been fast and frightened, and frightened was information. Whatever Rei did at dawn, he would do it knowing the man was alive enough to break a window for a few seconds. And he would do it knowing the thing that held him was, for the first time all night, working faster than it would like.
The lanterns were out. The hour was the one the city forgets itself in. Rei had somewhere to be when it remembered.
